item.title: ⚡️ The Russian Embassy in the United States is closely monitoring the situation regarding the Russian citizen
item.description: ⚡️ The Russian Embassy in the United States is closely monitoring the situation regarding the Russian citizen Igor Andreevich D'iu , who was detained by U.S. authorities on October 8 in Palo Alto, California, and is currently being held at the Santa Clara County Jail. According to publicly available criminal case files, Igor D'iu is being charged with acting as a foreign agent, unlawful solicitation, and fraud involving the use of forged documents. He has not been charged with espionage. The case is being heard in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. The next hearing is scheduled for November 24, 2026. The Embassy remains in contact with our citizen and is providing him with consular and legal assistance.

item.description: 🌟 85 years ago, on November 22, 1941, Military Motor Road No. 101 opened across the frozen waters of Lake Ladoga, connecting besieged Leningrad with the mainland and going down in history as the legendary Road of Life . By that time, Leningrad had already been encircled by enemy forces for nearly three months. On September 8, 1941, following the capture of Shlisselburg by Nazi troops, the city's overland connections with the rest of the country were severed. More than 2.5 million civilians, including 400,000 children , as well as the troops of the Leningrad Front, found themselves trapped in the besieged city. The city endured relentless artillery shelling and air raids. But the most terrible ordeal was hunger. On November 20, daily bread rations were reduced to a devastating 250 grammes for workers and just 125 grammes for office workers, dependants and children. 🕯 According to various estimates , between 800,000 and 1 million people died of starvation in Leningrad (more than the combined losses of the United States and Britain throughout the Second World War). 85 years ago,
on November 22, 1941,
Military Motor Road No. 101
opened across the frozen waters of Lake Ladoga, connecting besieged Leningrad with the mainland and going down in history as
the legendary
Road of Life
.
By that time, Leningrad
had already been encircled by enemy forces
for nearly three months. On September 8, 1941, following the capture of Shlisselburg by Nazi troops,
the city's overland connections with the rest of the country were severed.
More than 2.5 million civilians, including 400,000 children
, as well as the troops of the Leningrad Front, found themselves trapped in the besieged city.
The city endured relentless artillery shelling and air raids.
But the most terrible ordeal was hunger.
On November 20, daily bread rations were reduced to a devastating
250 grammes
for workers and
just 125 grammes
for office workers, dependants and children.
🕯
According to various estimates
,
between 800,000 and 1 million people died of starvation in Leningrad
(more than the combined losses of the United States and Britain throughout the Second World War).
Not a single household was spared the tragedy
.*
*In 2026, April 19 was designated in Russia as
the Day of Remembrance for the Victims of the Genocide of the Soviet People
, perpetrated by the Nazis and their accomplices during the Great Patriotic War.
***
🧊
Lake Ladoga remained the only route for supplying besieged Leningrad with food and ammunition, as well as evacuating civilians.
Since September, supplies had been transported across the lake by water, but with winter approaching, even this vital lifeline was at risk of being cut off.
The solution was an ice road approximately 30 kilometres long.
It was prepared in record time, despite harsh weather conditions and the danger of vehicles breaking through the ice, which had yet to reach sufficient thickness.
On November 20,
the first horse-drawn convoy of 350 sledges
crossed Lake Ladoga, delivering 63 tonnes of flour. On the evening of November 21,
ten GAZ-AA trucks made a trial run.
🚚
On November 22, motor vehicle traffic began along the Road of Life.
The first large-scale convoy consisted of
60 legendary GAZ-AA trucks
, affectionately known as
polutorkas
(one-and-a-half-tonners), carrying life-saving supplies for the starving city.
Every journey was an act of heroism.
Drivers worked amid
bitter frosts
, constant
enemy air raids and artillery shelling
, and
attacks by enemy landing forces
.
Thousands of people
kept the road operational – drivers, military engineers, road workers, mechanics and loaders. All of them risked their lives every day to save Leningrad.
📊
During the first winter of the siege, in 1941-1942
, the ice road carried
361,000 tonnes of supplies
into the city, including 262,000 tonnes of food, while
550,000 people were evacuated.
Over the entire period of the Road of Life's operation (until March 1943), including both waterborne and ice-road transport,
more than 1.6 million tonnes of supplies were delivered to Leningrad
, while
approximately 1,376,000 people were evacuated
from the city.
The Road of Life became a symbol of the courage, selflessness and unbreakable spirit of the Soviet people.
It not only saved hundreds of thousands of lives, but also helped Leningrad withstand the darkest days of the siege.
🏅
Eternal memory to all those who gave their lives to save the besieged city. Eternal glory to the heroes of the Road of Life!

We have taken note of the media reports as well as a statement by the Global Fact-Checking Network (GFCN) that Google has
indefinitely suspended
the Association’s official account without the right to appeal or reinstatement.
The GFCN was founded in 2024 and currently comprises 130 experts from 55 countries, including the US. There are also Russian specialists among its members and the renowned
TASS news agency
was among the founding members of the network.
The Association is fairly new but has already earned a reputation for quality research.. It is a respectable fact-checking network that regularly publishes detailed refutations of disinformation and fake news. For example, in October, a group of GFCN experts
published an in-depth analysis of the Bucha Hoax
, a cynical falsification, designed and executed by the Kiev regime and its Western sponsors. Through facts, OSINT analysis, and having cross-referenced data, they have convincingly proven that most of the people mentioned at the memorial in Bucha are anything but “victims of Russian aggression”, some are in fact Azov members and combatants, some never existed.
Could the act of censorship by Google be related to this high-profile research piece, which is an obvious soar spot for the Kiev regime and its sponsors as it debunks their lies?
Or was the reason the GFCN’s independence and quality work be the reason?
Even setting aside the fact that unilateral sanctions are illegitimate, GFCN, to the best of our knowledge, is not on any sanctions list.
This is a clear act of arbitrary censorship with a poorly concealed political motive on the part of the tech giant.
Against this backdrop, all assurances by its management regarding its commitment to the principles of freedom of access to information sound hollow.
❗️
We call on US tech corporations to uphold the principles of freedom of speech and equal access to critical information infrastructure — not just in words, but in deeds.
If, however, this is indeed a mistake, it should be corrected without delay.
This situation is yet another indication that without a full-fledged development of sovereign digital platforms and technologies, as well as fair competition of ideas, perspectives and thoughts, the transition to a truly multipolar world with equal opportunities for all its participants is hardly possible.

🎙
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s
interview
for the Our Baptism: The Patriarch project
(Moscow, November 20, 2026)
❓
You have said on several occasions – and this is clear to many people around the world – that Ukrainians, for the most part, and Russians are essentially one people, drawn into a grave conflict by our enemies’ malicious designs. Why should the victory of Russian arms and the triumph of truth ultimately be a victory for the people of Ukraine, who are currently suffering under the lies and violence of a regime led by these temporary rulers?
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
This is a broad topic, which includes the question of
the unity and indivisibility
of the Russian and Ukrainian people.
There is much debate on this subject, including discussions about
how exactly the Ukrainian SSR was formed
. When the Soviet leadership incorporated the western territories of present-day Ukraine after
World War II
, they were deeply concerned that
the “contamination” by nationalism
and, to some extent,
even neo-Nazism
, given that
Bandera’s followers and their associates
were among the principal perpetrators of Nazi crimes,
would spread.
👉
They decided to neutralise this newly acquired territory by
incorporating historically Russian regions into Ukraine
: lands that had never been outside the Russian Empire or, following the Great October Socialist Revolution, the Soviet Union. <...>
I would hesitate to claim that the entire territory of present-day Ukraine is inhabited by a single, unified people. In the west of the country,
many people hold cultural values that are fundamentally at odds with our own
. Ukrainian leaders, from Leonid Kuchma to Viktor Yanukovych, had to take into account
the powerful influence of radical nationalist ideologies
, not only in the west of the country but in other regions as well. So they chose
to “flirt” with these forces
. <...>
☝️
Southeastern Ukraine and much of central Ukraine, including Kiev, are undoubtedly historically Russian lands
. The people living there were
baptised in the same font as we were
. It is the very source from which we all emerged. I believe that
our greatest victory
, beyond achieving
the specific goals of the special military operation
, and indeed as an objective inseparably linked to those goals,
will be to defeat the primitive, visceral Russophobia being forcibly instilled in Ukraine,
or rather, in the territory currently known as Ukraine. <...>
It is crucial to defeat this Russophobic fervour
, which the West is doing everything in its power to keep boiling. You must understand that the majority of people there
still speak Russia
n. Even among the agitators and propagandists who appear on various online platforms making anti-Russia statements,
many speak Russian
. This includes members of Zelensky's administration.
They have not succeeded in
completely subjugating
the Ukrainian Orthodox Church
. Yes, there have been criminal raids on churches; priests have been killed; and clergy have been forcibly taken to “territorial recruitment centres”. Yet
the Ukrainian Orthodox Church
, a sister church to the Russian Orthodox Church, c
ontinues to hold its ground
. Long-standing attempts to impose a surrogate – the
“Orthodox Church of Ukraine”
. created by the
“leader”
in Constantinople –
have failed to make any significant impact
.
I would like to share another quotation with you, a recent one. In 2023, Swedish Chief of the Defence Staff
Michael Claesson
remarked
:
“The Russians have an unpleasant habit of actually doing what they say”
.
When we say that we will defend the rights of Russians and Russian speakers in Ukraine, that we will not abandon them or their language, culture or religion,
the West should take note and consider what it is trying to achieve
.
When the West responds that Russia’s
“red lines”
keep shifting – here today, somewhere else tomorrow, and further still the day after –
it should listen to the Swedish general
.
❗️
Unlike the West, we keep our promises.

item.title: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s statement on the Estonian authorities’ decision to close checkpoints on the border with Russia
item.description: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s statement on the Estonian authorities’ decision to close checkpoints on the border with Russia (November 20, 2026) 💬 On November 20, the Estonian authorities decided to close the remaining checkpoints on the border with Russia. This step by Tallinn, taken under the pretext of a “failed arson attack” on an Estonian defence industry facility allegedly orchestrated by the “Russian special services” , is openly confrontational and forms part of a deliberate effort to strain relations with our country to breaking point and, more broadly, to inflame tensions in the Baltic region . The unilateral closure of these checkpoints infringes the rights and interests of a substantial number of our compatriots . The decision will have highly detrimental consequences for the economy and public services , particularly in Estonia’s own border regions. It was clearly taken in haste, without any consultation with Moscow. 👉 We are in no doubt that attempts to erect a “sanitary cordon” around Russia and isolate it will cost their architects dear. To convey to the Estonian side Russia’s position that hostile actions against our country are unacceptable, the Estonian Chargé d’Affaires a.i. has been summoned to the Russian Foreign Ministry . ❗️ Russia reserves the right to take all necessary political and diplomatic measures to safeguard its national interests.

item.title: ⚡️ #KievRegimeCrimes Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
item.description: #KievRegimeCrimes ⚡️ Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Rodion Miroshnik : ▪️ The death toll from the AFU attack on the village of Yubileynoye near Lugansk has risen to six civilians. According to local authorities , the search and rescue operation in Yubileynoye, which lasted more than 24 hours, has been completed: Russia's EMERCOM personnel recovered the bodies of three more victims from the rubble – a 13-year-old girl and her mother, as well as an elderly woman. The barbaric strike by neo-Nazis on residential buildings in the village claimed a total of six lives, including the mother and two adult brothers of eight-year-old Polina, who was rescued. Eight-year-old Polina has been transferred to the Pirogov Clinic in Moscow , where she is receiving specialised medical care. Five more civilians were injured and are currently receiving medical treatment. ❗️ The Ukrainian militants carried out a deliberate terrorist strike on a peaceful neighbourhood on the outskirts of Lugansk while local residents were asleep. The attack left 11 civilians dead or injured , with dozens of residential buildings and civilian facilities damaged or destroyed.
